requirement: Distinguish variant effect, inheritance, remaining allele and current repair function.
sourceScope: Fictional examples test arithmetic or evidence interpretation; they are not clinical/model observations.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: BRCA1 and BRCA2 name genes everyone normally carries. Interpret a reported variant by its classification, sample and origin, then assess the remaining allele and repair function. An uncertain BRCA2 variant with no normal sample and no remaining-copy assessment establishes neither inheritance nor biallelic loss nor current repair deficiency. Tumor purity and complex copy-number states can limit allele interpretation.

requirement: Explain distinct BRCA1 coordination and BRCA2 RAD51-loading roles with model scope.
sourceScope: Fictional examples test arithmetic or evidence interpretation; they are not clinical/model observations.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: BRCA1 and BRCA2 have different repair roles. Brca1-deficient mouse embryonic stem cells had impaired homologous repair of defined chromosome breaks in Moynahan 1999. Purified full-length human BRCA2 promoted RAD51 assembly on single-stranded DNA in Jensen 2010. These model-specific results do not determine the effect of every human variant; the matching-template diagram omits many preparation and finishing steps.

requirement: Interpret carrier pathology proportions without a personal-risk forecast.
sourceScope: Fictional examples test arithmetic or evidence interpretation; they are not clinical/model observations.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: In the CIMBA analysis, the invasive-breast-cancer results included 3,797 BRCA1 and 2,392 BRCA2 carriers, with individual marker data available for varying subsets. Among tumors with relevant marker information, 68% in BRCA1 carriers and 16% in BRCA2 carriers were triple-negative. These are pathology proportions among cancers in mutation carriers, not the chance that an individual carrier develops cancer or that a person with triple-negative disease carries a BRCA variant. Age and ascertainment matter.

requirement: Retain repair restoration as one mechanism without an unselected frequency claim.
sourceScope: Fictional examples test arithmetic or evidence interpretation; they are not clinical/model observations.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Repair capacity can change after treatment. In the selected eight-person resistant metastatic breast cancer cohort of Waks 2020, four acquired definite or putative BRCA reversions; other mechanisms could restore repair too. A reversion can restore a disrupted reading frame, while old genomic patterns remain. This selected cohort does not establish a common or most-frequent mechanism across all breast cancers, and a single tissue or blood sample can miss heterogeneous reversions.

requirement: Distinguish DNA lesions, fixed mutations, checkpoint responses and completed repair.
sourceScope: Fictional examples test arithmetic or evidence interpretation; they are not clinical/model observations.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: A DNA lesion is a physical or chemical problem; a mutation is a lasting sequence change. Repair can remove damage before a mutation is fixed. Recognition and checkpoint signaling are responses to the problem, whereas successful repair, tolerated damage, arrest and death are separate outcomes. The lesson map therefore ends by measuring the outcome instead of assuming that the alarm completed the repair.

requirement: Map BER, NER, MMR, HR and end joining as selected nonexclusive repair jobs.
sourceScope: Fictional examples test arithmetic or evidence interpretation; they are not clinical/model observations.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Selected repair jobs address different problems: base excision begins by removing a damaged base, nucleotide excision removes a lesion-containing stretch, and mismatch repair corrects copying mismatches. Lindahl purified an E. coli enzyme that released uracil without cutting the DNA backbone, a specific early base-excision step rather than proof of all human repair routes. Double-strand breaks can use matching-template homologous repair or end joining. These are selected jobs, not exclusive assignments of every lesion to one pathway.

requirement: Interpret gamma-H2AX as a response with timing and controls.
sourceScope: Fictional examples test arithmetic or evidence interpretation; they are not clinical/model observations.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Gamma-H2AX is histone H2AX phosphorylated at serine 139. Rogakou 1998 observed a rapid response after experimentally induced double-strand breaks in mammalian systems. A microscopy focus is a response around damage, not direct sequencing of a break or a universal repair-failure test. In a fictional culture with a bulky lesion and increased gamma-H2AX, measure lesion removal over time with suitable controls before claiming nucleotide-excision failure, homologous repair deficiency or drug sensitivity.

requirement: Qualify platinum lesion types and coordinated crosslink repair.
sourceScope: Fictional examples test arithmetic or evidence interpretation; they are not clinical/model observations.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Platinum agents can form DNA crosslinks; interstrand links block strand separation and require coordinated repair machinery. The Fanconi pathway links DNA-processing activities, and homologous repair can contribute to resolving replication-associated damage. This does not mean every platinum lesion is an interstrand link or that every HR-deficient tumor responds. A repair mechanism, an observed drug effect and clinical benefit in a defined population need separate evidence.

requirement: Distinguish historical scars from present repair and drug benefit.
sourceScope: Fictional examples test arithmetic or evidence interpretation; they are not clinical/model observations.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Genomic scars are historical patterns in sampled tumor DNA. They can remain after a surviving population restores homologous repair, so a scar result is not a direct measurement of current function or a guarantee of drug benefit. DNA extraction consumes material; purity, ploidy estimation, segmentation, specimen quality and algorithm version affect the reported result. Counts are not percentages of cells whose repair has failed.

requirement: Define LOH, copy-neutral LOH, TAI and LST with original filters and study populations.
sourceScope: Fictional examples test arithmetic or evidence interpretation; they are not clinical/model observations.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Loss of heterozygosity means losing one parental version, with or without a reduction in total copy number. Abkevich 2012 counted LOH regions longer than 15 megabases but shorter than a whole chromosome in epithelial ovarian cancer analyses. Birkbak counted imbalanced regions reaching a telomere without crossing the centromere. Popova studied transitions between adjacent regions at least 10 megabases long in basal-like breast carcinoma. The original LST method estimated counts separately within each chromosome arm, excluding centromeric breaks, after filtering and smoothing variations smaller than 3 megabases. Segment filters and clinical score cutoffs are different rules.

requirement: Retain composite-score scale, cutoff origin and intended use from the original version.
sourceScope: Fictional examples test arithmetic or evidence interpretation; they are not clinical/model observations.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: A composite score can sum different scar features. Telli 2016 used the unweighted sum of LOH, telomeric allelic imbalance and large-scale transitions, with a predefined high-score boundary reported as 42 in the abstract, or a deleterious BRCA1/2 finding, in three platinum-containing neoadjuvant triple-negative breast cancer trials. The training population used to choose a boundary, the treated population used to test response, the assay scale and the intended use are different facts. A number on another assay cannot be read against this threshold without validation; a response association is not an interchangeable treatment-selection rule.

requirement: Work the 12/8 versus 12/14 Mb example without converting it to a clinical cutoff.
sourceScope: Fictional examples test arithmetic or evidence interpretation; they are not clinical/model observations.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: In a fictional, already filtered within-arm profile, a 12-megabase segment next to an 8-megabase segment fails the requirement that both neighbors be at least 10 megabases. A 12-megabase segment next to a 14-megabase segment meets that size component. This tests counting, not a 10-megabase deletion rule, present repair function or a clinical response cutoff. The original algorithm filters and validation population still apply.

requirement: Distinguish a gene finding, historical scar, current repair function and treatment evidence.
sourceScope: Fictional examples test arithmetic or evidence interpretation; they are not clinical/model observations.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: A repair-gene finding suggests a possible cause, a genomic scar records accumulated consequences, and a functional assay tests present behavior. A variant is not automatically damaging, loss of one copy is not automatically loss of both, and repair can recover while historical scars persist. None of these observations alone is the probability of clinical benefit.

requirement: Explain template-guided repair and appropriate cell-cycle context.
sourceScope: Fictional examples test arithmetic or evidence interpretation; they are not clinical/model observations.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Homologous recombination uses sufficiently matching DNA, often the sister chromatid after copying, to repair certain breaks. BRCA1 helps coordinate repair; BRCA2 helps RAD51 assemble on prepared single-stranded DNA to search and pair with a template. Template availability and cell-cycle state matter. In a fictional model with both functional BRCA2 copies lost, template-guided repair is impaired and alternative joining can leave deletions and rearrangements, but the sequence of a scar does not uniquely identify the cause or every protein that acted.

requirement: Specify RAD51 assay adequacy, damage and cycling-cell controls.
sourceScope: Fictional examples test arithmetic or evidence interpretation; they are not clinical/model observations.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: A low RAD51-focus count is interpretable only with adequate tumor cells, an appropriate cycling population and evidence that the cells experienced damage. Cruz 2018 assessed RAD51 with geminin as an S/G2 marker and gamma-H2AX as a damage marker in patient-derived models and retrospective tumor specimens. Fixed tissue can support this functional-surrogate approach; functional does not always mean live drug culture. An inadequate sample is uninformative, and a research assay needs analytical and clinical validation for its intended use.

requirement: Keep platinum trial associations and germline-label eligibility separate.
sourceScope: Fictional examples test arithmetic or evidence interpretation; they are not clinical/model observations.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Telli tested scar-score associations with response to platinum-containing chemotherapy before surgery in triple-negative breast cancer; that result does not establish a universal PARP-inhibitor cutoff. Farmer demonstrated sensitivity to PARP inhibition in BRCA-deficient cell models, a separate evidence setting. The U.S. olaparib early-breast-cancer label specifies deleterious or suspected deleterious germline BRCA findings, HER2-negative high-risk disease, prior neoadjuvant or adjuvant chemotherapy and companion-diagnostic selection. A tumor-only result or high scar score does not replace those criteria.

requirement: Distinguish signature inference from mutation cause and drug-response probability.
sourceScope: Fictional examples test arithmetic or evidence interpretation; they are not clinical/model observations.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: A mutational signature is a distribution over mutation categories inferred from a catalog of calls. It does not attach an observed cause to every mutation. Several processes can overlap, some causes remain unknown, and a classifier of BRCA-related repair deficiency is not a model of a patient's probability of drug response. Its endpoint and validation population must be named.

requirement: Explain SBS, DBS, indels and mixtures, and calculate the toy 50/50 and 60/40 reconstructions.
sourceScope: Fictional examples test arithmetic or evidence interpretation; they are not clinical/model observations.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Single-base substitutions change one base, doublet substitutions change adjacent bases, and indels insert or delete sequence. In a fictional four-category exercise, template A has percentages 40, 30, 20, 10 and B has 30, 40, 20, 10. For 100 mutations, a 50/50 mixture gives 35, 35, 20, 10; a 60/40 mixture gives 36, 34, 20, 10. The close reconstructions illustrate ambiguity; these are arithmetic examples, not fitted SBS3 data or observed biological results.

requirement: Preserve HRDetect six-feature and sequencing-platform scope.
sourceScope: Fictional examples test arithmetic or evidence interpretation; they are not clinical/model observations.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: HRDetect combines six weighted features, including microhomology-associated deletions, substitution signatures 3 and 8, rearrangement signatures 3 and 5 and a scar index. It is not simply an SBS3-positive call. In the original study, applying genome-trained weights to exome-like data reduced sensitivity to 46.8%; retraining improved it to 73% while adding calls not made by the genome model. Missing rearrangements and sparse substitutions are consequential, so panel, exome and whole-genome implementations require separate validation, uncertainty and fit checks.

requirement: Verify added APOBEC and HRDetect numerical claims against primary methods and cohorts.
sourceScope: Fictional examples test arithmetic or evidence interpretation; they are not clinical/model observations.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Roberts analyzed 954,247 mutations across 2,680 exomes from 14 cancer types; the APOBEC pattern reached 68% of mutations in some samples, not in every breast cancer. HRDetect reported 98.7% sensitivity and 124 high-scoring tumors among 560 breast cancers, about 22%, under its study definition. That selected cohort estimate is not a population prevalence or a clinical response probability. DNA quality, variant-calling errors, signature competition, catalog and software versions remain part of interpretation.

requirement: Distinguish compatible-end c-NHEJ, microhomology-associated joining and POLQ-mediated mechanism.
sourceScope: Fictional examples test arithmetic or evidence interpretation; they are not clinical/model observations.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Classical nonhomologous end joining reconnects ends without requiring a long matching template and can preserve compatible ends. Microhomology-associated joining uses short matching sequences after end processing. Theta-mediated end joining names a POLQ-mediated mechanism; finding short matches alone does not identify that enzyme. These routes overlap in outcomes without becoming interchangeable definitions.

requirement: Explain Ku and ligase IV versus resection and short-match alignment.
sourceScope: Fictional examples test arithmetic or evidence interpretation; they are not clinical/model observations.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Ku binds broken ends, and ligase IV with supporting factors can help align and seal them; difficult ends can require processing. Resection exposes single-stranded regions for alternative joining, where short matches can align and intervening sequence can be lost. Purified-factor experiments, defined chromosome-break reporters and controlled cellular studies test particular substrates and factor dependencies, not a universal menu for every break.

requirement: Count the toy 14-to-7 bp product, TTAA plus GAC loss and two nicks.
sourceScope: Fictional examples test arithmetic or evidence interpretation; they are not clinical/model observations.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: A fictional top-strand sequence CA-GAC-TT|AA-GAC-GT has 14 base pairs before joining. A selected short-match product CA-GAC-GT retains seven, losing the four-base TTAA interval and one three-base GAC repeat. In the pictured selected alignment, trimming the unmatched TT flaps leaves seven paired positions and two backbone nicks to seal, without a gap to fill. Other substrates can require synthesis; this arithmetic and schematic geometry are not measured repair frequencies.

requirement: Require perturbation and survival evidence before calling POLQ dependence.
sourceScope: Fictional examples test arithmetic or evidence interpretation; they are not clinical/model observations.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Sequence a repaired junction and measure a defined repair reporter, then perturb the proposed factor with specificity controls and, where feasible, rescue. Repair fraction, junction distribution and cell survival are distinct outputs. A deletion with microhomology is compatible with a joining route, but does not demonstrate POLQ dependence, selective killing or benefit from a POLQ inhibitor in a patient. Viable-cell and purified-component studies have model-specific input and material costs.

requirement: Distinguish fork slowing, checkpoint response, damage, recovery and survival.
sourceScope: Fictional examples test arithmetic or evidence interpretation; they are not clinical/model observations.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Replication stress concerns difficulty copying DNA, including slow or stalled forks. A stalled fork can be protected and restart; it is not automatically a broken chromosome. Checkpoint activation, recovery, incomplete copying, damage and death are separate stages and measurements. High checkpoint-gene RNA or rapid proliferation alone does not establish fork stress, dependence or drug sensitivity.

requirement: Explain RPA-ATRIP recruitment and model-specific oncogene/nucleotide effects.
sourceScope: Fictional examples test arithmetic or evidence interpretation; they are not clinical/model observations.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: RPA coats exposed single-stranded DNA and helps recruit ATR through ATRIP, initiating checkpoint signaling in biochemical and cellular experiments. Activated H-Ras in normal human-cell models produced hyper-replication before damage signaling and senescence. Bester studied HPV E6/E7 or cyclin-E-driven models in which nucleotide limitation disturbed replication and nucleoside supplementation in culture improved dynamics. These experiments do not recommend supplements or predict the behavior of every oncogene-bearing tumor.

requirement: Calculate 7.5 micrometres times 2 kb/micrometre divided by 30 minutes as 0.5 kb/min.
sourceScope: Fictional examples test arithmetic or evidence interpretation; they are not clinical/model observations.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: In a fictional DNA-combing exercise, live cells receive a 30-minute IdU pulse followed by a 30-minute CldU pulse. At the stated example stretching calibration of 2 kilobases per micrometre, a 7.5-micrometre second track represents 15 kilobases copied in 30 minutes, or 0.5 kilobases per minute; a 15-micrometre track gives 1 kilobase per minute. Bester used those pulse times and calibration, but these example lengths are not that study's results and the calibration is not universal.

requirement: Retain live-label input, calibration, track-selection and cell-cycle limits.
sourceScope: Fictional examples test arithmetic or evidence interpretation; they are not clinical/model observations.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: DNA-fiber measurements require viable cells that incorporate labels; extraction destroys sampled cells. Ordinary fixed pathology cannot retrospectively supply live-label tracks. Document pulse timing, labeling, stretching, track selection, cell-cycle distribution, model and comparison group. A lower population S-phase fraction is distinct from the speed of one selected molecule. Track length alone establishes neither the cause, breaks, restart nor death; checkpoint dependence needs a targeted perturbation and a separate functional outcome, without a universal patient-positive cutoff.

requirement: Distinguish AR staining, LAR classifier, functional dependence and clinical benefit.
sourceScope: Fictional examples test arithmetic or evidence interpretation; they are not clinical/model observations.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Receptor amount, location, transcription and growth dependence are different observations. Nuclear AR immunostaining reports protein in sampled cells; a luminal androgen receptor, or LAR, label is a versioned RNA-classifier result. TBCRC 032 correlative analyses found AR protein expression alone insufficient to identify AR-dependent tumors. Neither staining nor classifier membership alone proves patient benefit.

requirement: Explain ligand-binding versus DNA-binding regions and receptor-form context.
sourceScope: Fictional examples test arithmetic or evidence interpretation; they are not clinical/model observations.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Full-length AR has distinct regions for transcriptional regulation, DNA binding and ligand binding. Androgens can change receptor interactions, nuclear localization and regulatory-DNA binding, with effects determined by partners, accessible DNA and receptor form. Tran's antiandrogen experiments in prostate models tested binding, nuclear movement and transcriptional effects separately. An RNA signal does not characterize a truncated protein or transfer those prostate results to breast-cancer treatment.

requirement: Interpret discordant 20% IHC and non-LAR fictional findings.
sourceScope: Fictional examples test arithmetic or evidence interpretation; they are not clinical/model observations.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: A fictional tumor with 20% AR-positive nuclei but a non-LAR RNA classification need not have a mistaken result. The assays measure different layers; compare antibody, scoring, tumor-cell content, preservation, sampling, normalization and classifier version. Twenty percent stained nuclei is not twenty percent of patients expected to respond. Dependence requires a controlled receptor perturbation with downstream and growth or survival measurements.

requirement: Retain TNBCtype-4 tissue-mixture and prostate-versus-breast evidence boundaries.
sourceScope: Fictional examples test arithmetic or evidence interpretation; they are not clinical/model observations.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Lehmann 2016 refined TNBCtype from six classes to four tumor-specific classes after immune and stromal contributions explained the former immunomodulatory and mesenchymal stem-like signals. LAR does not mean estrogen-receptor-positive disease. TBCRC 032 was a defined phase Ib/II metastatic breast-cancer study of enzalutamide with or without taselisib, with phase II focused on AR-positive TNBC; its exploratory correlations do not turn an RNA subtype into a universal treatment rule or import a prostate indication.

requirement: Distinguish BET pocket engagement, protein depletion and clinical benefit.
sourceScope: Fictional examples test arithmetic or evidence interpretation; they are not clinical/model observations.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Engaging an acetyl-recognition pocket and depleting a whole protein are different interventions. In selected TNBC models with acquired BET-inhibitor resistance, cells remained dependent on BRD4 through bromodomain-independent regulation. Verify pocket engagement and depletion independently before comparing growth outcomes. Neither operation alone establishes clinical benefit or a vulnerability caused by an uncharacterized BET-family variant.

requirement: Explain acetyl-mark reader versus writer, BET family and extra-terminal functions.
sourceScope: Fictional examples test arithmetic or evidence interpretation; they are not clinical/model observations.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: BET proteins read acetylated lysine marks; they do not write the acetyl mark. The family includes BRD2, BRD3, BRD4 and BRDT, with two bromodomains and an extra-terminal interaction region. BRD4 can recruit transcription-elongation machinery, but other bromodomain proteins are not all BET proteins and family members are not functionally interchangeable. The lesson figure retains the histone mark during pocket occupation and depletion; its representative pocket does not claim JQ1 is BD1-specific.

requirement: Interpret continued probe growth with controlled BRD4 depletion sensitivity.
sourceScope: Fictional examples test arithmetic or evidence interpretation; they are not clinical/model observations.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: In a fictional culture, an engaged BET pocket probe leaves growth unchanged while independently controlled BRD4 depletion impairs growth. The findings can coexist if the remaining protein supplies functions the probe does not block, as the resistant-model work illustrates. Binding assays, chromatin occupancy, early RNA changes, later growth and death, general transcription effects and appropriate restoration controls answer different questions. Lower MYC RNA alone does not attribute a later effect to MYC.

requirement: Verify NUT fusion and four-patient clinical report without extrapolating to ordinary variants.
sourceScope: Fictional examples test arithmetic or evidence interpretation; they are not clinical/model observations.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: French identified a BRD4-NUT fusion in the defined carcinoma; a fusion is a different biological alteration from an ordinary sequence variant. Stathis reported four people with confirmed BRD4-NUT carcinomas treated with OTX015/MK-8628 in compassionate use: two had rapid regression, with no randomized comparison or established survival benefit. The report described thrombocytopenia, including reversible grade 3 events and a grade 4 event in one patient. This small selected series does not establish efficacy across BET-altered tumors.

requirement: Distinguish allele, downstream activity, dependence and context-dependent inhibitor direction.
sourceScope: Fictional examples test arithmetic or evidence interpretation; they are not clinical/model observations.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: The exact allele and intervention matter. In chemical-genetic cell experiments, ATP-competitive RAF inhibitors could increase ERK signaling through RAS-dependent RAF dimer transactivation in wild-type-BRAF settings. Reduced downstream phosphorylation, growth dependence and clinical benefit are separate endpoints. A pathway name or RNA score cannot identify the upstream driver or predict the direction of an inhibitor effect.

requirement: Explain GTP/GDP RAS switch and RAF-MEK-ERK relay.
sourceScope: Fictional examples test arithmetic or evidence interpretation; they are not clinical/model observations.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: This MAPK branch relays signals from receptor and other inputs through the GDP/GTP RAS switch to RAF kinases, MEK and ERK. RAS is a GTP-binding switch; RAF, MEK and ERK are protein kinases. Moodie examined active-RAS complexes, and Kyriakis tested Raf-1 activation of MAP kinase kinase. These defined experiments support steps in the relay; other MAPK branches exist and the simplified map omits regulators.

requirement: Interpret reduced phospho-ERK with unchanged growth using specificity controls.
sourceScope: Fictional examples test arithmetic or evidence interpretation; they are not clinical/model observations.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: A fictional compound that lowers phospho-ERK within an hour without changing growth has demonstrated a sampled downstream biochemical effect, subject to assay controls. It has not alone proved direct target binding, attributed growth dependence or patient benefit. Specify the allele, protein site, total-protein normalization, preservation, exposure, timing and cell population, then confirm engagement and functional effects with independent perturbations and appropriate controls.

requirement: Retain alternative inputs, feedback and nonunique upstream attribution.
sourceScope: Fictional examples test arithmetic or evidence interpretation; they are not clinical/model observations.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Shared inputs, branches and feedback can alter the magnitude or even direction of a perturbation response over time. High pathway-associated RNA is not a universal activity meter, and a changed ERK site cannot identify a sole upstream receptor. Davies' BRAF work established transforming activity for specific mutations in defined models, not a common effect for every uncertain BRAF variant. Drug selection still needs its own allele-, disease- and setting-specific evidence.

requirement: Distinguish copy gain, RNA, protein, gene program and dependence.
sourceScope: Fictional examples test arithmetic or evidence interpretation; they are not clinical/model observations.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Copy gain, RNA abundance, protein amount, chromatin binding, a transcriptional program and functional dependence are separate layers. MYC pairs with MAX for sequence-specific DNA binding. A high RNA level or subtype association alone does not establish that disrupting MYC will selectively impair the sampled cancer.

requirement: Explain MYC-MAX pairing and direct versus indirect transcription effects.
sourceScope: Fictional examples test arithmetic or evidence interpretation; they are not clinical/model observations.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: MYC helps regulate programs involving growth, metabolism and proliferation through partners and regulatory context. Sabo's mouse and cultured-cell work separated selective gene regulation from broader RNA increases accompanying altered cell state; direct binding and indirect transcription effects are not equivalent. Normalize for cell composition, proliferation and RNA per cell before assigning a MYC mechanism to a gene-expression pattern.

requirement: Interpret a broad growth-inhibitory compound without assigning the effect to MYC.
sourceScope: Fictional examples test arithmetic or evidence interpretation; they are not clinical/model observations.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: In a fictional sample with high MYC RNA, unmeasured protein and growth suppression by a broadly acting compound, MYC dependence remains unresolved. Confirm the relevant cells and MYC disruption, use independent perturbations, appropriate restoration and normal-cell comparisons, and measure growth and death separately. General transcriptional damage or many changed messages does not attribute the compound's effect to MYC.

requirement: Retain normal-tissue, selected TNBC-model and indirect BET-intervention scope.
sourceScope: Fictional examples test arithmetic or evidence interpretation; they are not clinical/model observations.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Horiuchi compared MYC-related patterns in human TNBC and tested CDK-inhibitor vulnerabilities in selected models; it did not establish dependence in every patient. Soucek used reversible genetic MYC inhibition in a Ras-driven mouse lung-cancer model and observed tumor regression alongside effects on normal regenerating tissues. Delmore showed JQ1-associated MYC transcription reduction in myeloma models. Genetic MYC inhibition, BET inhibition and a particular medicine's exposure, safety and clinical benefit remain different evidence settings.

requirement: Distinguish receptor amount, received signaling, cell identity and growth dependence.
sourceScope: Fictional examples test arithmetic or evidence interpretation; they are not clinical/model observations.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: A ligand-bearing sender, receptor amount, received signal and growth dependence are separate observations. Locate malignant, vessel and other neighboring cells before assigning a Notch mechanism. Ligand on a vessel is not evidence that the tumor received the signal, and total receptor is different from a released nuclear intracellular domain.

requirement: Explain neighbor contact, extracellular cut, gamma-secretase cut and nuclear NICD.
sourceScope: Fictional examples test arithmetic or evidence interpretation; they are not clinical/model observations.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Common contact-dependent Notch signaling begins when Delta-like or Jagged ligand on one cell engages a receptor on a neighbor. Ligand-regulated extracellular cleavage permits subsequent gamma-secretase-mediated membrane cleavage; the released Notch intracellular domain, NICD, can enter the nucleus and work with transcriptional partners. This route differs from an RTK phosphorylation relay and omits receptor maturation and sender mechanics.

requirement: Retain activating T-ALL versus inactivating squamous-cancer allele context.
sourceScope: Fictional examples test arithmetic or evidence interpretation; they are not clinical/model observations.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Weng found activating NOTCH1 changes in extracellular heterodimerization or PEST regions in more than half of the studied T-ALLs. Agrawal identified predicted inactivating alterations in head-and-neck squamous tumors, suggesting a tumor-suppressor role there. An uncharacterized allele inherits neither direction from the pathway name; tissue, cell identity and alteration effect matter.

requirement: Interpret ligand-independent fictional activation and broad inhibitor limitations.
sourceScope: Fictional examples test arithmetic or evidence interpretation; they are not clinical/model observations.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: A fictional T-ALL culture with high nuclear NICD without a ligand-bearing neighbor, and lower NICD after gamma-secretase blockade, supports a ligand-independent activation hypothesis. A contact-blocking experiment that lowers NICD without changing growth instead supports reduced received signaling without demonstrating a growth requirement. Control general toxicity, contact conditions, independent pathway perturbations and compensation. Gamma-secretase also processes other proteins; responsive HES/HEY RNA and nuclear staining need validated assays and are not universal eligibility cutoffs.

requirement: Distinguish KEAP1-CUL3 regulation, NRF2 output, protection and dependence.
sourceScope: Fictional examples test arithmetic or evidence interpretation; they are not clinical/model observations.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: NFE2L2 encodes NRF2, a transcription factor; KEAP1 is an adaptor linking it to a CUL3-containing ubiquitin-ligase complex. Under suitable unstressed conditions, tagging promotes NRF2 degradation. Reduced turnover can make more NRF2 available for nuclear stress-defense programs. Protein turnover, nuclear output, protection against a stressor and survival dependence require separate measurements.

requirement: Explain reduced turnover without universal physical release and CUL3 substrate breadth.
sourceScope: Fictional examples test arithmetic or evidence interpretation; they are not clinical/model observations.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Zhang's biochemical and cell experiments found stress-associated inhibition of NRF2 ubiquitination without disruption of every KEAP1-NRF2 association. The lesson's paired conditions depict altered turnover, not creation of NRF2 or a mandatory physical latch release. CUL3 is a scaffold used with other adaptors and substrates, so a CUL3 change cannot be assigned an NRF2 effect from its name alone.

requirement: Interpret restoration and NRF2 perturbations with defined stress outcomes.
sourceScope: Fictional examples test arithmetic or evidence interpretation; they are not clinical/model observations.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: In a fictional culture, high NQO1 RNA, nuclear NRF2, several responsive proteins and reduced readouts after controlled KEAP1 restoration support a regulatory consequence. Test survival under a defined stress separately, using a specific NRF2 perturbation, matched controls and appropriate restoration to assess dependence. Stronger defenses may confer resistance; their abundance does not demonstrate ferroptosis sensitivity or benefit from an NRF2-directed therapy.

requirement: Verify lung-cohort proportion and brusatol general translation effects.
sourceScope: Fictional examples test arithmetic or evidence interpretation; they are not clinical/model observations.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Singh sequenced 54 non-small-cell lung tumors and found KEAP1 mutations in ten, about 19%, alongside a separate 12-cell-line analysis. This cohort proportion is not a universal lung-cancer prevalence. Vartanian's proteomic study in A549 and other cell experiments found that brusatol broadly inhibited protein synthesis, so lower NRF2 after that compound does not establish selective engagement. Use cell identity, preservation, timing, several outputs and general-translation controls; no universal NRF2-high treatment cutoff follows.

requirement: Distinguish lipid/protein phosphorylation, feedback response, growth dependence and recycling.
sourceScope: Fictional examples test arithmetic or evidence interpretation; they are not clinical/model observations.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Class I PI3K phosphorylates a membrane lipid, producing PIP3; PTEN removes its position-3 phosphate. AKT and mTOR are protein kinases. A PIP3 lipid result and an AKT1 Ser473 phosphosite result are therefore different molecular measurements. Document specimen preservation, cell mixture, protein site, timing, exposure, comparator and total-protein normalization before interpreting a change as activity or dependence.

requirement: Explain PTEN, PDK1 Thr308, mTORC2 Ser473 and indirect TSC2-RHEB route.
sourceScope: Fictional examples test arithmetic or evidence interpretation; they are not clinical/model observations.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Membrane recruitment helps organize AKT activation. PDK1 phosphorylates AKT1 Thr308, whereas the rictor-mTOR complex supplies Ser473 phosphorylation in the defined experimental route. AKT can inhibit TSC2, relieving the TSC1/2 brake on RHEB, which promotes mTORC1 signaling. The diagram's indirect AKT-to-mTORC1 connection stands for these regulatory steps; it is not direct phosphorylation of mTORC1 by AKT.

requirement: Retain mTORC1/2, autophagy initiation versus flux, and S6K1-IRS1 feedback.
sourceScope: Fictional examples test arithmetic or evidence interpretation; they are not clinical/model observations.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Raptor-containing mTORC1 and rictor-containing mTORC2 are distinct complexes. mTORC1 regulates protein production and autophagy-initiation machinery; releasing initiation restraint is not proof of completed recycling flux. Harrington linked S6K activity to reduced IRS-1 function, and O'Reilly observed increased IRS-1 and AKT signaling after RAD001 in cell models and treated tumors. Feedback release can change an output without proving that a combination improves outcomes in every setting.

requirement: Keep capivasertib population/companion-diagnostic eligibility and fictional phosphosignal exercise separate.
sourceScope: Fictional examples test arithmetic or evidence interpretation; they are not clinical/model observations.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: In a fictional mTORC1 perturbation, lower production-regulator phosphorylation followed by higher AKT1 Ser473 and unchanged growth supports biochemical changes, not essentiality or failed engagement; timing alone does not prove the feedback connection. Test the proposed wiring and functional outcome independently. The FDA's 2023 capivasertib-with-fulvestrant approval specified adults with hormone-receptor-positive, HER2-negative advanced breast cancer, qualifying PIK3CA/AKT1/PTEN alterations on an approved test and specified prior endocrine treatment or early recurrence. It is not a TNBC indication inferred from a pathway label.

requirement: Distinguish receptor amount, phosphorylation, target engagement, dependence and benefit.
sourceScope: Fictional examples test arithmetic or evidence interpretation; they are not clinical/model observations.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Receptor amount, phosphorylation, direct drug engagement, growth dependence and clinical benefit are separate observations. Lower receptor phosphorylation supports a biochemical effect under the assay conditions but can also reflect indirect regulation; it does not by itself prove direct binding. A controlled functional effect with independent specificity tests is needed before assigning receptor dependence.

requirement: Explain family-specific activation arrangements and FGFR helper-molecule scope.
sourceScope: Fictional examples test arithmetic or evidence interpretation; they are not clinical/model observations.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Many RTKs have extracellular ligand-binding regions, membrane-spanning regions and intracellular tyrosine-kinase machinery. Families activate differently: Zhang demonstrated an asymmetric EGFR kinase-domain interaction, while Stauber examined an FGF1-FGFR2 extracellular complex with a proposed heparin-related assembly arrangement. Ligand, helper molecules, receptor member and context matter. A downstream phosphosite can have multiple upstream causes and is not a universal receptor meter.

requirement: Verify HER2 1987 cohort and randomized 2001 clinical endpoint claims.
sourceScope: Fictional examples test arithmetic or evidence interpretation; they are not clinical/model observations.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Slamon 1987 studied 189 primary breast cancers and reported HER2 amplification in 30%, associated with relapse and survival; that historical study is not a present-day universal prevalence or a causal drug-response experiment. In the 2001 randomized trial of 469 women with HER2-overexpressing metastatic breast cancer, adding trastuzumab to chemotherapy increased median survival from 20.3 to 25.1 months, with cardiac toxicity as a material risk. A trial median summarizes a group and does not predict an individual survival time.

requirement: Avoid inferring direct drug binding from a phosphosignal or dependence from one uncontrolled growth assay.
sourceScope: Fictional examples test arithmetic or evidence interpretation; they are not clinical/model observations.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: In a fictional comparison, two cultures contain a receptor, but only the amplified, high-surface-protein culture slows growth after a blocking antibody, while receptor phosphorylation falls in both. This separates amount, sampled signaling and growth response; the pattern suggests dependence but attribution still needs controls and independent perturbation. RNA is not surface accessibility, a family-name inhibitor need not engage every member at the tested exposure, and For an antibody-drug conjugate, receptor access and payload delivery are separate questions from whether growth requires that receptor's signaling. Fixed-tissue staining and viable-model perturbation have different input costs and validation scopes.

requirement: Distinguish canonical output, ligand dependence, functional dependence and response.
sourceScope: Fictional examples test arithmetic or evidence interpretation; they are not clinical/model observations.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Canonical pathway output, dependence on secreted Wnt, growth dependence and clinical response are separate claims. Nuclear beta-catenin can reflect pathway signaling, whereas total beta-catenin also includes adhesion functions. Lower AXIN2 RNA supports an output effect with suitable controls, not selective killing or patient benefit. Wnt routes that do not use beta-catenin are outside this canonical readout.

requirement: Explain destruction control, nuclear versus adhesion beta-catenin and PORCN upstream step.
sourceScope: Fictional examples test arithmetic or evidence interpretation; they are not clinical/model observations.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Canonical Wnt uses Frizzled with LRP5/6 co-receptor machinery. Without an effective signal, the Axin/APC-organized destruction machinery and sequential kinase steps promote beta-catenin degradation; signaling can change that control and allow nuclear regulation with partners. PORCN supplies a lipid modification required for proper Wnt secretion in the studied systems. Blocking that upstream step need not overcome a downstream escape from destruction control.

requirement: Interpret the two fictional upstream-block/downstream-escape cultures.
sourceScope: Fictional examples test arithmetic or evidence interpretation; they are not clinical/model observations.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Two fictional cultures have nuclear beta-catenin. Secretion blockade reduces the nuclear signal in culture A but not in culture B, where downstream bypass is stipulated. A supports a ligand-dependent hypothesis; B illustrates how an upstream block can leave a downstream output intact. The symbols represent qualitative readouts, not protein counts or a real drug dataset. Neither pattern alone establishes selective killing; measure viability and control intervention specificity.

requirement: Specify assay preservation, AXIN2/reporters, model controls and lack of universal treatment cutoff.
sourceScope: Fictional examples test arithmetic or evidence interpretation; they are not clinical/model observations.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Assays can measure localization, AXIN2 RNA or a defined transcriptional reporter, before and after a specified perturbation. Preservation, composition, global transcription effects, model validation and tissue consumption matter; there is no universal Wnt-high treatment cutoff. In Rodon's phase 1 WNT974 study of 94 people with advanced solid tumors, AXIN2 fell in many paired biopsies while no RECIST responses were observed. Target-related output and tumor response must therefore be reported separately, alongside safety rather than a claim of demonstrated benefit.
